fixes.explanation: That's right, baker. The text says, "…David ordered that they be burned in the fire." (1 Chronicles 14:12). The Philistines had abandoned those gods there, and David gave the order about them. Fire was the answer.

Right, it's false. The text says, "…David again inquired of God…" (1 Chronicles 14:14). Having won once, he asked again anyway. God answered with a plan: don't march up after them, but circle around and attack in front of the balsam trees.

That's right. God said the sound would mean "…that God has gone out before you to strike the camp of the Philistines." (1 Chronicles 14:15). David was told to listen for it. The sound in the treetops was a sign that God was already on the move.

Yes, true. The text says, "…David did as God had commanded him…" (1 Chronicles 14:16). He followed the plan and the signal he was given. They struck down the Philistine army all the way from Gibeon to Gezer.

That's it, baker. The verse says, "And David’s fame went out into every land, and the LORD caused all nations to fear him." (1 Chronicles 14:17). His fame went out into every land. The part about the nations fearing him is the LORD's doing.

Yes, baker, a palace for David. Hiram, king of Tyre, sent envoys, cedar logs, stonemasons and carpenters to build it (1 Chronicles 14:1). That's a whole crew showing up at the door, and some of us can't even get a repair person to call us back.

A sensible guess, since a leader might gather his people. But the text says David "…inquired of God…" (1 Chronicles 14:10), and it doesn't mention him calling his leaders together. He asked whether he should go up against the Philistines. Asking God is what the text shows him doing.
Yes, their gods. The text says, "There the Philistines abandoned their gods…" (1 Chronicles 14:12). They left them there at Baal-perazim, where David had defeated them.
That's not what the verse says, baker. It says the Philistines "…abandoned their gods…" at Baal-perazim (1 Chronicles 14:12). A king isn't mentioned in this passage.

Yes, baker. God said, "As soon as you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, move out to battle…" (1 Chronicles 14:15). Hear the sound, then go. Think of the moment your oven timer dings and you reach for the mitts.

Close, since God did tell David to wait for something. But what he waited for was the sound: "As soon as you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, move out to battle…" (1 Chronicles 14:15). The text doesn't mention morning.
